Bare SBA-15 shows characteristic ordered channels without any surface coating, with the pore structure clearly visible and pore walls appearing smooth and uniform (Figure 14a). In contrast, the PA-coated sample shows clear formation of a thin, continuous coating layer at particle surfaces with thickness of approximately 20 nm (Figure 14b). The coating appears as a darker contrast layer surrounding the lighter SBA-15 support, uniformly distributed across the observed areas. The coating's uniform thickness and continuous nature indicate successful interfacial polymerization at the pore mouth without excessive bulk polymerization that would create thicker, irregular coatings or block pore entrances completely. Figure 14. TEM images of SBA-15 without coating (a) and with PA coating (b). To understand the thermal properties and composition of the coated materials, FTIR and derivative TGA were performed on various components and sorbents (Figure 15a and b). For convenience, samples were designated as TX-Y where X represents TMC concentration (wt.%) and Y represents solution-to-sorbent mass ratio (e.g., T2-0.5x indicates 2 wt.% TMC with 20 corresponding ratio of 0.5x). All samples show peaks at 450 cm-1 (Si-O-Si bending), 800 cm-1 (Si- O-Si symmetric stretching) and a strong peak at 1070 cm-1 (Si-O-Si asymmetric stretching). The TAPA/SBA-15 sample reveals new peaks around 3280 and 3360 cm-1 as the doublet for primary amines (N-H stretching), 1600 cm-1 (N-H bending), 813 cm-1 (N-H wagging). The selected coated sample (T2-0.5x) notably reveals new amide peaks at 1645 cm-1 (Amide I: C=O stretching), 1540 cm-1 (Amide II: N-H bending/C-N stretching), 1293 cm-1 (Amide III: C-N stretching/N-H bending), confirming the formation of PA linkages through the interfacial polymerization reaction. Pure TAPA shows an evaporation range from 100-235°C with maximum mass loss rate at approximately 200°C, confirming its high volatility at temperatures relevant to DAC regeneration. Bare SBA-15 shows no significant mass loss across the entire temperature range (100-800°C), serving as an inert support baseline. TAPA-loaded SBA-15 shows a broad feature similar to pure TAPA centered around 180°C corresponding to TAPA thermal evaporation from the pore structure. The T2-0.5x sample exhibits two additional broad decomposition features at approximately 215-350°C and 400-650°C that are absent in the uncoated material. These features align with those observed in pure PA synthesized separately from TMC and TAPA (225-330°C and 420-650°C), confirming the presence of PA coating in the T2-0.5x sample. The lower-temperature feature (215- 350°C) likely corresponds to decomposition of lightly crosslinked PA species and oligomers, while the higher-temperature feature (400-650°C) is attributed to degradation of the more extensively crosslinked PA network.24 Notably, the initial TAPA evaporation peak (100-200°C) in T2-0.5x shows similar intensity to the uncoated sample despite the presence of the coating.
